$comment: AP6 — the DEPENDENCY manifest, and the reason this example ships a SUBDIRECTORY. A `path` dependency must have a `.dss-project.json` AT THE ROOT of the named directory or the build fails loud with D_DependencyManifestNotFound (0xD019); there is no upward search and no 'bag of sources' fallback. `sources` is relative and re-bases against THIS directory (plan 06 §5.1 B.3), so `scale.c` is found here and never in the consumer's tree.
$commentProfile: `module` is the profile whose composition verb is SourceMerge (core/types/artifact_profile.hpp) — WHEN CONSUMED, the dependency contributes SOURCES and its artifact is ignored entirely; they are compiled WITH the consumer's. c-subset declares `module` in its own artifactProfiles list, which is the dependency's OWN language gate (a language that did not declare it would be rejected here, not in the consumer). ★ A `module` is nonetheless A LIBRARY as a PROJECT (operator ruling 2026-08-15): it declares `targets[]` and builds standalone like any other library, which is what makes it type-checkable, codegen-testable and diagnosable on its own instead of only inside whatever consumer first imports it. `artifactProfile` says what a project builds ITSELF as; `DependencyComposition` says how it is CONSUMED. The two are orthogonal, and only the CONSUMPTION path emits nothing.
$commentTargetsAreNotConsulted: ★ `targets[]` IS REQUIRED BY THE LOADER AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT ONE OF THE CONSUMER'S SPECS. Plan 06 §5.1 B.10: a dependency's own `targets[]` is NOT consulted when it is built as a dependency — it states the platforms the project builds FOR ITSELF, which is a different statement from 'which platforms this code can support'. The spec below is named by NO consumer target (the consumer names four `-exec` formats, none of them this one), so a resolver that regressed to consulting it could not stay green here. ⚠ MEASURED 2026-08-15 over all 24 `src/dss-config/object-formats/*.format.json`: `module` is served by the TEN library formats — every format that serves `lib` (5: dyn/dylib/dll) or `staticlib` (5: the archives) — so this key is a REAL standalone-build target, not the inert placeholder it was when `module` was served by nothing. It names an archive format because a standalone module builds as a library; the static-vs-dynamic choice is made here, by the target spec, exactly as it is for `lib` vs `staticlib`.
